title: Projective spreading and normalization after a purely inseparable generic extension
statement: Let $S$ be either the spectrum of a field or an excellent integral trait [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $Y$ be an excellent integral scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme] with a projective [def-kun-projective] dominant morphism $Y\to S$, and let $X_0$ be an excellent integral scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme] with a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant morphism $g:X_0\to Y$. Let $K/\kappa(Y)$ be a finite purely inseparable extension [def-sc-function-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then there exist an excellent integral scheme $Y_1$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme], a finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], projective [def-kun-projective], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], dominant morphism $b:Y_1\to Y$ with $\kappa(Y_1)\cong K$ and with $Y_1\to S$ projective [def-kun-projective], and an excellent integral scheme $X_1$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme] obtained as the normalization [def-sc-normalization] of a dominant irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_0\times_Y Y_1$ [def-pc-fibre-product], together with proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant morphisms $c:X_1\to X_0$ and $f:X_1\to Y_1$ satisfying $g\circ c=b\circ f$. The map $c$ is generically finite (finite over a dense open) [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $X$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:X_0\to X$ is a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant generically finite morphism, then $a\circ c:X_1\to X$ is proper, dominant and generically finite. At the generic point $y_1$ [def-sc-generic-point] of $Y_1$, the fibre $(X_1)_{y_1}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is the normalization of the corresponding dominant component of $(X_0)_{\eta}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(Y)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], where $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point] is the generic point of $Y$.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(Y)$. Construct $Y_1$ as the normalization of $Y$ in $K$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]: over $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ its coordinate ring is the integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in $K$. Here $A$ is an excellent domain and $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]; excellence of $A$ holds for every affine open $U$, since $Y$ is covered by affine opens with excellent rings [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover]. By [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], $A$ is Nagata; taking the prime $(0)$ in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] says it is N-2, and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] therefore says $A'$ is a finite $A$-module. Thus $b:Y_1\to Y$ is finite, directly by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The rings $A'$ are normal domains with fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]. The overlap identifications are the integral-closure localization identifications [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. In particular, localizing $A'$ at $A\setminus\{0\}$ gives the integral closure of $k$ in $K$, which is all of $K$. Hence $b^{-1}(\eta)=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $Y_1$ is integral, its function field is $K$ compatibly with $k$, and $b$ is dominant.

Each $A'$ in Step 1 is a finite type algebra over the excellent ring $A$, so it and all its localizations are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. The opens $b^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ cover $Y_1$, so every affine open of $Y_1$ has excellent ring [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover]: $Y_1$ is excellent. The finite map $b$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The base $S$ is affine and Noetherian in both allowed cases: a field is Noetherian, and a discrete valuation ring is Noetherian by the trait hypothesis. The given $Y\to S$ is H-projective [def-kun-projective] and proper [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type and in particular quasi-compact [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; so it is projective in the convention [def-pc-projective-morphism] that [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] requires. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to this $Y\to S$ and the finite $b$. Its affine-base conclusion gives a global closed immersion $i:Y_1\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$, with $Y_1\to S$ equal to the projection composed with $i$, and thus $Y_1\to S$ is projective in the required convention [def-kun-projective].

proof.text: The map $Y\to S$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Consequently $Y_1\times_S Y\to Y_1$ is proper, hence separated, by [lem-kun-proper-stability] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its section $\Gamma_b=(1,b):Y_1\to Y_1\times_S Y$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. The product $i\times1_Y:Y_1\times_S Y\to\mathbf P^N_S\times_S Y$ and its composite with $\Gamma_b$ are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. The target is $\mathbf P^N_Y$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback], and the composite followed by its projection is $b$. This is precisely a projective-space embedding over $Y$ [def-kun-projective], proving the projectivity of $b$ as well as the projectivity over $S$ already established.

Let $V=X_0\times_Y Y_1$, with projections $p:V\to X_0$ and $q:V\to Y_1$, and let $x_0$ be the generic point of $X_0$. Dominance of $g$ makes $F=\kappa(X_0)$ an extension of $k$. By Step 1 the fibre $p^{-1}(x_0)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_k K)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring] with the Noetherian local $k$-algebra $A=F$ and maximal ideal $(0)$. It says this fibre has exactly one prime, whose residue field $E$ is finite over $F$. Write $z$ for its point. Any generization of $z$ in $V$ still maps to $x_0$ and hence lies in this one-point fibre, so equals $z$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], every irreducible closed subset containing $\overline{\{z\}}$ has a generic point generizing $z$, and therefore equals $\overline{\{z\}}$. Thus this closure is an irreducible component. Give it its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and denote the resulting integral scheme by $W$ [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its generic point is $z$ with field $E$. It dominates $X_0$, and its image in $Y_1$ contains $y_1$: indeed $z$ lies over $\eta\in Y$ and $b^{-1}(\eta)=\{y_1\}$. Hence it dominates both factors.

proof.text: The projection $p$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] applied only to the finiteness of $b$; no radicial property of $b$ is asserted. The inclusion $j:W\hookrightarrow V$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Hence $p_W=pj$ is finite by the composition clause of [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. On an affine inverse-image chart it is a finite type algebra over an excellent affine coordinate ring of $X_0$; [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] therefore makes these chart rings excellent, and since the charts cover $W$, every affine open of $W$ has excellent ring [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover]: $W$ is excellent. Also $q$ is proper, being a base change of $g$, by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. Its restriction $q_W=qj$ to the closed subscheme $W$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper].

Take $n:X_1=W^
u	o W$, the normalization in $E=\kappa(W)$ [def-sc-normalization]. On every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq W$, $B$ is an excellent domain. Apply [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], take the prime $(0)$ in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], and use [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] with the degree-one extension $E/E$. The integral closure $B^
u$ is finite over $B$. It is a domain with fraction field $E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]. Consequently $n$ is finite and dominant; $X_1$ is integral, and it is excellent: the finite $B$-algebras $B^
u$ are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and the charts $\operatorname{Spec}B^
u$ cover $X_1$ [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover]. Set $c=p_Wn$ and $f=q_Wn$. The composition theorem [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] makes $c$ finite. The maps $n$ and $c$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and $f$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. Both maps are dominant: the generic point of $X_1$ maps to $z$, which maps to $x_0$ and $y_1$ by Step 4. The fibre-product identities give $gc=bf$. In particular $c$ is finite on all of $X_0$, and hence satisfies the stated generic-finiteness assertion.

proof.text:
Identify $V_{y_1}$ with $(X_0)_\eta\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The closed integral subscheme $W_{y_1}$ is a component of this fibre: on affine charts it is obtained from the minimal prime defining $W$ by inverting the nonzero elements of an affine coordinate ring of $Y_1$. That prime avoids these elements since $W\to Y_1$ is dominant; its localization is minimal, because a smaller prime would contract to a smaller prime before localization. The localized domain still has fraction field $E$. More explicitly, over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y_1$ put $T=R\setminus\{0\}$ and take an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq W$ mapping there. Dominance makes $T\to B$ consist of nonzero elements. The two normalization rings are
$$T^{-1}(\overline B^{\,E})\quad\text{and}\quad\overline{T^{-1}B}^{\,E},$$
and they agree by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. These canonical identifications agree on overlaps by the same localization statement. Using the affine construction [def-sc-normalization], they identify $(X_1)_{y_1}$ over $W_{y_1}$ with its normalization. This proves the required generic-fibre clause, including the map to the corresponding component.

Finally suppose the additional map $a:X_0\to X$ is given. The composite $ac$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. Since $c$ is proper and dominant, its closed image is all of $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]; hence $(ac)(X_1)=a(X_0)$ is dense in $X$, so $ac$ is dominant. Choose the dense open $U\subseteq X$ on which $a$ is finite, as supplied by the generic-finiteness hypothesis. The map $c$ restricted over $a^{-1}(U)$ is finite by the base-change clause of [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]; its composition with the finite $a^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite by the composition clause of the same node. Thus $ac$ is finite over the same dense open $U$.
